summary.text: The hypergeometric distribution covers draws without replacement from a finite population, where each result falls into one of two categories such as pass or fail.
Because each draw shrinks the population, the probability of a success changes on every draw.
A typical case is an urn of 5 green and 45 red marbles, drawing 10 without replacement and asking for exactly 4 green.

facts.label: Sampling type
facts.value: Without replacement from a finite population

facts.label: Two categories
facts.value: Each result is one of two exclusive groups, like pass or fail

facts.label: Matching test
facts.value: The hypergeometric test equals a one-tailed Fisher's exact test

facts.label: One-draw case
facts.value: With a single draw it becomes a Bernoulli distribution

items.prompt: You pull marbles out of an urn and keep each one out. Why does the chance of drawing a green one change from draw to draw?

options.label: Marbles change colour while in the urn
The urn is shaken harder each time
Each draw removes a marble, which shrinks the population
Green marbles are heavier and sink

items.explain: Sampling without replacement from a finite population means each draw decreases the population, so the success probability changes.

items.prompt: An urn holds 5 green and 45 red marbles, and you draw 10 without looking. Which is more likely: exactly 4 green or all 5 green?

options.label: Exactly 4 green, by a wide margin
All 5 green, since green is the focus
They are about equally likely
Neither can happen with only 10 draws

items.explain: Getting all 5 green among the 10 drawn is far harder; it is roughly 35 times less likely than getting 4.

items.prompt: Each item drawn from a pool is sorted into one of two exclusive categories. Which pair of categories fits?

options.label: Low, medium or high
Red, green or blue
Pass or fail
Any whole number from 1 to 80

items.explain: The results fall into two mutually exclusive categories, as with pass or fail.

items.prompt: You draw 10 raffle tickets from a bin of 40, putting each ticket back before the next draw, and count the winners. Which distribution describes that count?

options.label: Hypergeometric distribution
Geometric distribution
Multivariate distribution
Binomial distribution

items.explain: Drawing with replacement gives the binomial distribution; the hypergeometric one is for draws without replacement.

items.prompt: A lab finds k cells of one type in a sample and tests whether that type is under-represented. What does the p-value measure?

options.label: The chance of randomly drawing k or more of that type
The chance of randomly drawing k or fewer of that type
The chance of randomly drawing exactly k of that type
The chance of drawing none of that type at all

items.explain: In a test for under-representation, the p-value is the probability of randomly drawing k or fewer successes.

items.prompt: A marketing group wants to know whether a subgroup, such as people under 30, is over-represented among its known customers. Which approach fits?

options.label: A hypergeometric test
Counting customers by age and reporting the largest group
Checking whether each customer bought more than once
Asking each subgroup to vote on its share

items.explain: The hypergeometric test is often used to identify which sub-populations are over- or under-represented in a sample, including testing customers for over-representation of demographic subgroups.
